subject: math
verificationNotes: Hand-authored; numeric answers checked with sympy.
intro: A sample is a subset of a population used to estimate population characteristics. A simple random sample (SRS) gives every group of the same size an equal chance of selection. Other probability methods include stratified (divide into homogeneous strata, sample within each), cluster (sample whole groups), and systematic (every kth individual). Bias is systematic error that makes estimates miss the truth: voluntary response and convenience samples tend to overrepresent certain opinions, and undercoverage or nonresponse can also bias results.

items.prompt: A researcher numbers all 500 students and uses a random number generator to pick 50. Name the method.

steps: Every student has a known, equal chance, and every group of 50 is equally likely.
That defining property is a simple random sample.

items.prompt: A school is split into grade levels, and 10 students are randomly chosen from EACH grade. Name the method.

steps: The population is divided into groups (grades) that are internally similar.
A random sample is taken within each group.

items.prompt: An online poll reports that 80% support a change, based only on people who chose to respond. What bias is likely?

steps: Only people with strong opinions tend to answer voluntary online polls.
So voluntary response bias is likely.
Picking every kth individual is systematic.

items.prompt: Whole randomly chosen classrooms are surveyed entirely. Method?

steps: Sampling intact groups is cluster sampling.

items.prompt: Surveying only friends is what kind of (biased) sample?

steps: Easy-to-reach people form a convenience sample.
